PDF Selection Colors customizes temporary text-selection colors in Zotero’s PDF reader. It is intended for readers who want to adjust the background color of selected text. The repository is hosted under the GitHub account PeterBenjaminZhu.
Main features # The plugin offers an Everforest green preset, five Morandi presets, a custom color picker, and adjustable opacity. Settings are saved automatically and applied immediately to open PDFs. The color settings apply to temporary text selections; text, equations, figures, existing annotations, highlights, and underlines retain their original colors.
The default is the green preset at 25% opacity. A slider and numeric input support values from 0% to 100%. Restore Defaults returns to the initial colors. Disabling the plugin restores the reader’s original selection appearance; enabling it again restores the saved settings.
Compatibility and getting started # The source README identifies 1.0.6 as the current version and permits use with Zotero 10. It records checks of actual PDFs, old installer cleanup, and restart behavior on Windows with Zotero 10.0.7. macOS, Linux, and every Zotero 10 version have not been individually verified; Zotero 11 requires separate checks.
Visit the GitHub repository and follow the usage instructions to download and install the plugin, then adjust colors through Zotero’s Tools menu. The README also explains automatic updates and the optional old installer cleanup feature, which is disabled by default.
Source and license # Information checked on November 16, 2026, using a fixed source revision. The project uses the MIT License. Check the repository’s latest instructions and compatibility information before use.
summary: Customize temporary text-selection colors in Zotero’s PDF reader with color presets, a custom color picker, and adjustable opacity.
title: PDF Selection Colors

practical-tech-guides collects practical guides to programming languages, libraries, software tools, and website building, with independently runnable examples. The repository is hosted under the GitHub account PeterBenjaminZhu. The guides are primarily in Chinese and retain English technical names.
Main contents # The xAct basics guide is intended for readers familiar with basic Mathematica operations and introductory General Relativity. It introduces xTensor, xCoba, and independent Notebook examples. Each Notebook contains its complete calculation code for reading and execution step by step.
Personal website from scratch is intended for readers without website development experience. A HugoBlox teaching example explains content authoring, mathematics and references, bilingual pages, and manual GitHub Pages publication.
Prerequisites and getting started # Open the relevant guide from the GitHub repository. Check its environment, dependencies, and execution instructions before running an example. The source README distinguishes actual execution, independent mathematical review, and graphical application checks; consult each guide’s verification links for its recorded status.
When downloading the whole repository, preserve its directory structure so that chapters, examples, and instructions remain linked. Run each Notebook in a separate, clean kernel, evaluating it from the beginning in order. If messages appear or evaluation remains incomplete, check dependencies and execution order. The guides and Notebooks currently have no PDF versions.
Source and license # Information checked on November 16, 2026, using a fixed source revision. Original material uses the MIT License. Third-party software remains subject to its own licenses.
summary: Practical guides to programming languages, libraries, software tools, and website building, with independently runnable examples.
